CarTrade Tech (CARTRADE) · The story so far From a small car site to India's biggest used-goods marketplace, and the bet to earn more from the same users. How it got here • 2010: started as CarTrade, an online car marketplace • 2016: bought CarWale and BikeWale, the car and bike research sites • 2018: bought 51% of Shriram Automall, which auctions vehicles for banks and lenders • 2021: listed on the stock market • Aug 2023: bought OLX India for ₹523 Cr, shut the loss-making car-buying arm that came with it, and moved OLX onto its own tech in 3 months instead of 6 • FY24 to FY26: revenue went from ₹490 Cr to ₹779 Cr while costs grew far slower, so margins rose from about 9% to over 30%. Without OLX, underlying growth was about 16% a year What it is today • CarWale/BikeWale: new-car research, paid about 70% by car makers and 30% by dealers • OLX India: used goods, with about 63% of used-car listing value • Shriram Automall: vehicle auctions (about 55% owned) • 92–100% of visitors arrive without paid ads The bet Earn more from the same users instead of buying new ones: charge OLX buyers for the first time (Elite Buyer), premium plans for sellers, verified listings, car loans with IDFC FIRST and a retail tie-up with Spinny. Management's targets: ₹1,000 Cr profit in 4–5 years (about 4x FY26) and a "40-40" goal (40% profit growth, margins above 40%). The record 3 of 4 financial promises met, 1 slip in 13 dated ones. The miss: OLX growth was meant to speed up in Q4 FY26 and didn't, because a product launched 45 days late. OLX then grew 29% in Q1 FY27, against a weak quarter a year earlier. What the documents also show • Growth is slowing: revenue +16% in Q1 FY27, from 19–25% through FY26. Consumer visitors +7%, auction volumes flat. Profit still rises because each user earns more • The edge is OLX's buyer–seller network, not brand or lock-in. Open risks: AI search taking CarWale's Google traffic, and Facebook Marketplace • Other income, mostly interest on ₹1,321 Cr of cash, is about 30% of pre-tax profit. The tax rate was 16% in FY26 and is heading to 23–24% (already near 24% in Q1 FY27). Return on equity is about 10%, which management agrees is below its cost of capital because of the cash • On our valuation check, today's price implies about 41% earnings growth a year over the next few years, above the broker forecasts we hold (about 25–37%) What to watch 1. Do OLX business buyers pay, or leave, as charging rolls out? 2. Can OLX hold 25%+ growth against normal comparisons? 3. Does the 31% Q1 margin keep rising through FY27, as management guides? Jyoti CNC and Macpower CNC make the same machines in the same city. Macpower's own CMD says they share "a same product basket, same distribution network".

Jyoti has the better record on paper: revenue up 31% a year over three years against 18%, at a 25% margin against 16%. But over FY22-26 Jyoti turned ₹750 Cr of profit into minus ₹18 Cr of operating cash. Macpower turned ₹109 Cr into ₹36 Cr.

FY27: Jyoti's plant is full and its new block, re-dated three times, is due this week. Macpower is filling a plant it already owns.

The prices: Jyoti implies about 45% earnings growth a year, above our bull case of 31-38%. Macpower about 38%, at the top of our base case.

Which risk would you rather own: an oven not yet lit, or one that must run hotter?

TD Power Systems: ₹192 cr order for US gas-turbine generators, its first for a 2-pole design. Deliveries run Aug 2027 to Jan 2028. Which of these was already on your radar? Q2 FY27 results tracker is live Results season is on, and you can now follow it in one place: every company we cover by board-meeting date, with each concall scored as it lands. 8 scored so far. The standout is Transformers & Rectifiers (TARIL) at 6.7. My takeaway from the call: demand isn't the constraint. They have ~₹21,000 Cr of inquiries under negotiation, almost 3x their ₹7,237 Cr order book, and see no price war because "everybody has enough orders in hand." Nuclear (a first NPCIL order), data centres and BESS are opening new pockets on top. The catch: FY27 guidance was held at 25%+ even after H1 grew 35%, and the new Changodar plant slipped from August to Diwali. Open the tracker Not investment advice.

The Leela, Q2 FY27: RevPAR +30%, almost all of it from room rates; occupancy flat at 68.8%. ConcallScore 6.9, provisional until the official transcript is filed. Full read: The Leela on Story of a Stock

E2E Networks, Q2 FY27: revenue up 410% on a year ago, yet the ConcallScore still came out at 5.8 (provisional). That's the duality I want to highlight. Why: the growth was expected. Q2 was the first full quarter of the GPUs that went live in June, and the monthly run-rate moved only 4.6% from there, so there wasn't much positive change. The next B200 lot slipped, and management dodged the Q&A on what the new ~₹1,000 Cr contract adds. Maybe a slightly strict outcome, but that's what the score reads. Story continues. The GPU renting business is doing great for them, as you can see. Personally I'm not a big believer in the platform play they are targeting, but let's see how it plays out as they try to go upstream. Full read: E2E Networks on Story of a Stock

SG Finserve, Q2 FY27: the loan book is up 98% on a year ago to ₹5,694 Cr, already past the ~₹5,500 Cr it guided for the whole of FY27. ConcallScore 7.4 (provisional). Why not higher: profit rose only 9% on the quarter. Borrowing now funds the growth (debt is 2.7x net worth, against a 3x ceiling), and interest costs climbed with it. Management also called Q2's growth front-loaded, and sidestepped questions on digital-lending returns and the RBI draft rules. Still, the best score of the season so far: 7.4 is the highest of the 14 Q2 calls we've scored. Full read: SG Finserve on Story of a Stock

HFCL concall: what a banger. 1. The MD said it himself: "it is always good to be conservative. Give you a lower number and surprise you by better numbers." That's exactly what this call was. The FY27 growth guide went from 40% to at least 80%, a positive rate of change. 2. Same with margins. One analyst sounded shocked at how high they were. The MD's reply: repeatable, and "going to get better only". 3. Everything got a positive spin. The one worry raised, data centres funded with debt as the cost of capital rises, became a pitch that AI demand isn't going away. 4. The long game: it looks like the optical fibre boom is funding aerospace and defence (radars, drone detection, niche and high-margin), ready to take over when the fibre story plays out in a year or two. Medium term looks great, and they're planning for the long term too. What a call. A must-listen. ConcallScore 8.0 (provisional), the highest of the 15 Q2 calls we've scored. Full read: HFCL on Story of a Stock

An order-and-capacity week: two big order wins, three plants or plans moving, and one order book running behind its own target. Top announcements this week (17 – 24 Oct): 1. Welspun Corp: its US arm won a ~₹5,500 cr firm order for coated line pipes on a Permian gas pipeline feeding a hyperscaler data centre complex. It executes in FY29, so it adds nothing to FY27 or FY28: US demand was already booked well through FY28. 2. Quality Power: manufacturing started at the new Sangli coil factory on 20 Oct, with a ramp-up as more lines are commissioned. In August the company had targeted trial production for that month. The plant carries a ₹1,500-1,800 cr peak revenue potential. 3. Venus Pipes: part of the ~₹70 cr pipe spooling facility is running, ahead of the December 2026 timeline. Spooling was guided at ~5% of FY27 top line. 4. Pitti Engineering: the board approved ₹450 cr capex to take sheet metal capacity from 1,08,000 MT to 1,60,000 MT and consolidate the Karnataka lamination units into one facility, phased up to FY2030-31. 5. Transrail: ₹927 cr of fresh orders, mostly 765kV and 400kV transmission lines. That takes FY27 order intake to ₹3,356 cr against a ₹10,000-11,000 cr guide, with 6 of 12 months over. Which of these do you think changes the company's year the most? You can always check the latest top announcements on the Filings page. Notes from company filings, not investment advice.

Steel Strips Wheels, Q2 FY27: revenue up 61% to ₹1,930 Cr, EBITDA up 110% to ₹235 Cr, and profit tripled to ₹119 Cr. The ConcallScore agrees this time: 7.7 (provisional, off a third-party transcript). Why it scored well: volumes grew with a richer alloy mix, H1 is already ahead of the FY27 guide (revenue +44% against 20% plus), exports are recovering, and the board approved a ₹1,400 Cr greenfield for alloy and steel wheels. What held it back: about ₹140 Cr of the quarter's revenue is catch-up billing on repriced orders, and three analysts could not get a clean answer on how much of it reached EBITDA. The bigger story is aluminium overtaking steel as the growth engine. Full read, with the one-page poster: Steel Strips Wheels: The sign over the door says steel Not investment advice.

Ather Energy, Q2 FY27: revenue up 63% to ₹1,464 Cr, EBITDA positive for a second quarter at 4.9%, and its first quarterly profit after tax. The ConcallScore: 7.3 (provisional, off a third-party transcript), Bullish but a notch below Q1's 7.5. Why it scored well: pre-orders doubled, gross margin held at 24% through a 9.4-point commodity hit, and the board approved capacity to about 11.4 lakh units by Q2 FY28. What held it back: Hosur is full, so market share slipped to 15.1% from 17.2% while the industry grew 82%, and management said 2.7 points of the margin gain is a temporary lever. The bigger story is supply, not demand. Full read, with the one-page poster: Ather Energy: A queue out the door, and the kitchen already full Not investment advice.
